notes: All signals below are real OpenTitan UART RTL signals; every id was resolved by sv_query against the opentitan_uart snapshot.
Ground truth was established by reading the RTL source under hw/ip/uart/rtl and hw/ip/prim/rtl and cross-checked with the recorded sv_query CLI commands.
The snapshot stores the signal graph but NOT source text: file/line evidence (T3) requires re-running with --filelist (or --file) instead of --from-snapshot.

tasks.question: In the OpenTitan UART block, look at the internal register-block signal that gates the write-enable of the interrupt-test (INTR_TEST) registers. What single signal drives it, and which nine register write-enable signals does it feed? Then look at one of those write-enable signals in turn: which two signals drive it, and does anything load it?

answer.empty_side_note: This is the empty-side case: the signal has 2 drivers and 0 loads (it is a register-file output port, so nothing downstream consumes it inside the UART).

source_confirmation.detail: logic intr_test_qe; logic [8:0] intr_test_flds_we; assign intr_test_qe = &intr_test_flds_we; then 'assign reg2hw.intr_test.<field>.qe = intr_test_qe;' for each of the 9 INTR_TEST fields.

tasks.ground_truth_command: sv_query drivers --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.u_reg.intr_test_qe' --json ; sv_query loads --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.u_reg.intr_test_qe' --json ; sv_query drivers --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.u_reg.reg2hw.intr_test.tx_watermark.qe' --json ; sv_query loads --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.u_reg.reg2hw.intr_test.tx_watermark.qe' --json

tasks.question: Trace the directed (dataflow) path inside the OpenTitan UART from the chip-level receive pin input to the 16-bit shift register that accumulates the incoming byte. Which signals does the data pass through on the way, and how many hops is the path?

answer.path_canonicality_note: The 18-hop path is the --canonical selection (policy max_nodes_then_lexicographic). WITHOUT --canonical, `paths --directed` returns a 9-hop path for the same pair, and `paths --all` enumerates 48 distinct directed paths (hop counts 10..19). The ground-truth command therefore pins --canonical.
answer.physical_stages: cio_rx_i -> uart_core.rx port -> prim_flop_2sync (2-stage synchronizer) -> rx_sync -> rx_sync_q1/rx_sync_q2 (majority-vote filter) -> rx_in_maj -> rx_in_mx (noise filter mux) -> rx_in (loopback mux) -> rx_val_q (16-bit shift register)

source_confirmation.detail: The RTL confirms the same order: prim_flop_2sync sync_rx -> always_ff rx_sync_q1/q2 -> assign rx_in_maj/rx_in_mx -> assign rx_in -> always_ff rx_val_q <= {rx_val_q[14:0], rx_in}.

tasks.ground_truth_command: sv_query paths --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.cio_rx_i' 'uart.uart_core.rx_val_q' --directed --canonical --json ; sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"path","from":"uart.cio_rx_i","to":"uart.uart_core.rx_val_q"}' --json

verification.expected_output: paths (WITH --canonical): found=true hop_count=18 candidate_count=48; verify claim status=verified. WARNING: without --canonical, paths --directed returns hop_count=9 for the same pair.

tasks.question: Find the exact source location in the OpenTitan UART where the 16-bit receive shift register is updated, and quote the statement that loads a new received bit into it. In which file and at which line(s) does that happen, and what is the surrounding always/if structure?

answer.tooling_caveat: trace evidence and graph subgraph --evidence need --filelist/--file; the saved snapshot carries the graph only, so file/line evidence is null when queried via --from-snapshot.

tasks.ground_truth_command: sv_query trace evidence --filelist /tmp/opentitan_svq/opentitan.f 'uart.uart_core.rx_val_q' --json ; sv_query graph subgraph 'uart.uart_core.rx_val_q' --filelist /tmp/opentitan_svq/opentitan.f --depth 1 --direction both --evidence --json

verification.expected_output: trace evidence: source_location.file='uart_core.sv', line_start=306, line_end=306, source_text="if (!rst_ni)            rx_val_q <= 16'h0;"; enclosing_always spans lines 305-308 of uart_core.sv; subgraph edges carry hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_core.sv:307 and :308

tasks.question: Two claims were made about the OpenTitan UART register block. Claim A: the sticky integrity-error output of the register block is driven by the sticky error flop in the same block. Claim B: that integrity-error output feeds the UART's fatal-alert request. Verify or refute each claim against the design, and also check whether the receive-line signal could possibly drive the TX output register (it should not).

negative_control.reason: uart.uart_core.rx_in is not in fanin(uart.uart_core.tx_out_q, depth=1)

source_confirmation.detail: logic err_q; always_ff ... err_q <= '0; else if (intg_err || reg_we_err) err_q <= 1'b1; ... assign intg_err_o = err_q | intg_err | reg_we_err;  -> claim A holds.

source_confirmation_B.detail: uart_reg_top u_reg (... .intg_err_o (alerts[0]) );  -> claim B holds; alerts[0] then drives prim_alert_sender.alert_req_i.

tasks.ground_truth_command: sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"driver","signal":"uart.u_reg.intg_err_o","driver":"uart.u_reg.err_q"}' --json ; sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"path","from":"uart.u_reg.intg_err_o","to":"uart.alerts[0]"}' --json ; sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"driver","signal":"uart.uart_core.tx_out_q","driver":"uart.uart_core.rx_in"}' --json

verification.expected_output: claim A status=verified; claim B status=verified; negative control status=contradicted with reason 'uart.uart_core.rx_in is not in fanin(uart.uart_core.tx_out_q, depth=1)'

tasks.question: Someone claims there is a directed dataflow path in the OpenTitan UART from the chip-level TX output pin all the way back to the internal TX output register, and also asks whether a signal named 'uart_core.nonexistent_sig' feeds the receive shift register. Check both: is the TX-to-TX-register path real, and does the missing signal exist at all?

case_1_missing_signal.cli_level_behavior: sv_query paths --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.uart_core.nonexistent_sig' 'uart.uart_core.rx_val_q' --directed --json  => ok=false, error='signal id not found in graph', unknown=['uart.uart_core.nonexistent_sig'], hint="用 `svq graph nodes --json` 列出可用 id"

case_2_no_directed_path.explanation: There is no directed (dataflow) path from the TX output pin back to the TX output register: tx_out_q drives tx, and tx drives cio_tx_o, so the direction is the other way round. The reverse direction IS structurally connected, which is why the tool reports reverse=True.
case_2_no_directed_path.correct_direction: uart.uart_core.tx_out_q -> uart.uart_core.tx.ternary_line_loopback -> uart.uart_core.tx -> uart.cio_tx_o (3 hops, verified directed)

answer.conclusion: The 'nonexistent_sig' endpoint does not exist in the design, so the path claim cannot be evaluated (unknown, not contradicted). The TX-pin-to-TX-register claim is false in the directed sense (contradicted).

tasks.ground_truth_command: sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"path","from":"uart.uart_core.nonexistent_sig","to":"uart.uart_core.rx_val_q"}' --json ; sv_query paths --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.uart_core.nonexistent_sig' 'uart.uart_core.rx_val_q' --directed --json ; sv_query verify claim --from-snapshot opentitan_uart --claim '{"type":"path","from":"uart.cio_tx_o","to":"uart.uart_core.tx_out_q"}' --json ; sv_query paths --from-snapshot opentitan_uart 'uart.uart_core.tx_out_q' 'uart.cio_tx_o' --directed --canonical --json

verification.expected_output: missing-signal claim status=unknown with reason 'endpoint unresolved'; paths CLI returns ok=false 'signal id not found in graph'; reverse-direction claim status=contradicted with reason 'path check failed (forward=False, reverse=True)'; forward direction tx_out_q->cio_tx_o found=true hop_count=3
